dataPolicy: Public repository summary and rendered report/presentation assets only. Live Kalshi credentials, private keys, and raw API access are not bundled into the portfolio.

thoughtProcess.title: Define a market response window
thoughtProcess.body: Use ESPN play-by-play win-probability jumps as event anchors, then inspect Kalshi one-minute prices around each shock.

thoughtProcess.title: Build leakage-safe sequences
thoughtProcess.body: Group train/test splits by game and represent each shock-market pair as a fixed-length OHLCV sequence so models cannot memorize games across splits.

thoughtProcess.title: Separate overreaction from slow updating
thoughtProcess.body: Compare the market price move against the win-probability shock to distinguish rare large overreactions from the more common underreaction pattern.

thoughtProcess.title: Compare tabular and sequence models
thoughtProcess.body: Benchmark logistic and linear baselines against LSTM and Transformer models that can use the full local price path.

figures.title: Win probability shock vs. market move
figures.alt: Scatter plot comparing ESPN win-probability shocks with Kalshi price changes around NBA events.
figures.caption: Most market moves do not scale cleanly with shock size, and true one-minute overreactions are rare.

figures.title: Mispricing classification
figures.alt: Classification figure distinguishing underreaction, efficient response, and overreaction windows.
figures.caption: The labeling frame separates slow updates from genuine overreactions rather than treating every price gap as the same kind of error.

figures.title: Held-out event sequence
figures.alt: Line chart comparing model predictions with true post-shock market price for a held-out event.
figures.caption: Sequence models track the immediate post-shock price path more closely than tabular baselines.
